messages:
Maya (Customer): Hey Redwood — starting ~08:12 UTC we saw a spike of 504s when hitting your hosted /v1/generate endpoint. ~30% of requests during the window failed, our users complaining about timeouts. Can you advise?

Emma (Support): Sorry about that, Maya. Can you share a couple request IDs or a sample curl we can repro with? Also which model and region?

Maya (Customer): region: us-west-2, model: rwd-base-16k, request id: req_8b3f2c (from our logs). Payloads are short (prompt ~40 tokens). Example curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"rwd-base-16k","input":"Summarize: ..."}'```

Emma (Support): Thanks. Tagging oncall. @raj can you take a look at gateway metrics for req_8b3f2c window?

Raj (Oncall): I'm on it. Pulling ingress/gateway dashboards now. Seeing a sharp rise in request-queue-length starting 08:10 — queue depth went from ~40 -> 800 across hosted pool us-west-2. p95 latency for the gateway jumped to ~3.8s, and there's a concurrent increase in batcher backlog.

Tia (Infra): That smells like continuous-batching backlog. Do we have batcher loop timings? Looking at batcher telemetry: batch_window_ms was default 20ms but effective accumulation indicates batch sizes ballooned to 256+ and kv-cache memory pressure causing some hosts to drop connections.

Carlos (SRE): Logs show our request-queue early-rejects started firing but threshold was high. I see many `gateway: 502 upstream reset` and `worker: timeout waiting for kv fetch` in the same timeframe. Pasting excerpts: 
```
[08:11:23] gateway: accept req=req_8b3f2c route=/v1/generate queued=612
[08:11:24] batcher: dispatching batch size=276 target=512 latency_ms=3200
[08:11:25] worker: ERROR req=req_8b3f2c upstream=worker-42 err=kv_cache_timeout
[08:11:26] gateway: respond req=req_8b3f2c status=504
```

Raj (Oncall): We also see `continuous_batcher_pending` metric spike and `batch_window_effective_ms` increasing — likely because the system is auto-extending batching to meet throughput and that extended queuing is causing tail timeouts for short prompts.

Emma (Support): Is this a tenant spike or system-wide? Maya — did you ramp traffic or change concurrency?

Maya (Customer): No intentional ramp. We've got normal traffic but the errors started suddenly. We saw a couple of retries from our side.

Tia (Infra): It appears a noisy tenant (different customer) caused a sustained high batch size in the shared hosted pool. When continuous batching accumulates large batches, latency for early requests in the batch suffers. Our default queue depth and batching policy didn't early-reject soon enough.

Carlos (SRE): Mitigation options: 1) immediate: increase gateway early-reject aggressiveness for that pool (lower max_queue_size), 2) reduce continuous_batcher_max_batch_size or cap effective batch window to keep per-request latency bounded, or 3) failover some traffic to dedicated pool. I'm leaning on (1) + (2) for short term.

Raj (Oncall): I'm going to flip a temporary policy: set pool(us-west-2).max_queue_size=200 and continuous_batcher.max_batch_size=128. Will monitor.

DeployBot: deployment triggered by raj:infra — changed config pool(us-west-2).max_queue_size -> 200, continuous_batcher.max_batch_size -> 128 (conf diff id: cfg-3141)

Tia (Infra): Config change active. Watching ingress and batcher metrics.

Carlos (SRE): Also enabling per-tenant backpressure so noisy tenant gets early-rate-limited. Patch applied to routing policy for noisy-tenant-id 0x9f.

Raj (Oncall): After change, queue depth dropped from ~800 -> ~150 within 30s. p95 gateway latency dropped to ~420ms and 504s fell to baseline. Flicker of 502s during transition but it stabilized.

Emma (Support): Maya — can you confirm if your failed requests are now succeeding?

Maya (Customer): Confirmed — error rate back to normal since ~08:14. Thanks! Will monitor for the rest of the day.

Carlos (SRE): Root cause notes for now: continuous batching autogrew due to a noisy tenant saturating pool; queue depth hit limits and backpressure/early-reject thresholds were high so tail latency/timeouts manifested as 504s. Secondary cause: kv-cache timeouts on memory pressured hosts leading to upstream resets (502/504).

Tia (Infra): Action items:
- Short term: adjust default pool config to lower max_queue_size and limit continuous_batcher.max_batch_size (done as emergency change).
- Mid term: add dynamic tenant isolation heuristics + automatic early-reject based on tail-latency signals.
- Long term: expose per-tenant 'latency-sensitive' route that disables large-batching, with an SDK flag for customers who want low tail-latency.

Carlos (SRE): Also adding a postmortem draft and capturing metrics and request-ids for the window. Will include config diffs and timeline.

Emma (Support): Maya, we'll follow up with a summary and the postmortem link when ready. Sorry again for the disruption. :heart:

Maya (Customer): Appreciate the quick response — thx everyone.

Raj (Oncall): Filing incident ticket INC-2141599999. I'll add graphs (ingress queue length, batch size, p95) and the specific request IDs.

DeployBot: incident INC-2141599999 created by raj (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2141599999)

Carlos (SRE): Postmortem draft created and assigned. Planning to run a replay test in staging that simulates noisy-tenant with sustained large open requests to validate new defaults.

Tia (Infra): We'll also add alert rule: if continuous_batcher_pending > 300 for > 1m then trigger auto-limiter to reduce pooling window and notify SRE.

Emma (Support): Marking this thread resolved for the customer side; keeping internal followup in the incident.

Maya (Customer): Resolved for us. Thanks!
